meta.name: Little Rambles Developmental Map
meta.verificationStatus: FRAMEWORK-DERIVED, NOT EXPERT-VERIFIED (debt D2, Phase 0 gate review 2026-07-27). Band structure and skills derived from the cited frameworks; affordance weights are provisional product inventions. Professional review by an early-childhood educator or pediatric OT is required before this map is exposed to families beyond the founder (scheduled: Phase 2, before Phase 3 beta). Until then, treat all weights as hypotheses. EXTENSION 1.1.0 (2026-07-27, ADR-0012): bands 42-60 and 60-84 added; 60-84 exceeds CDC checklist coverage (AAP/dev-psych derived) — treat as lower-confidence pending D2 review. EXTENSION 1.2.0 (session 2): affordances vehicle_watch, snow_play, food_ritual, group_program added with per-band weights to close transit/winter/food/community-program coverage gaps.
editorialRules: NOT DIAGNOSTIC: This map describes emerging skills (opportunities), never expected achievements (judgments). No content may imply a child is behind.
Milestones are wide ranges. Band boundaries are soft; children straddle bands constantly and that is normal.
Serve-and-return framing: every affordance description should center caregiver-child interaction, not passive exposure.
When sources disagree or evidence is thin, prefer the more conservative, lower-pressure claim.
Refresh procedure: re-check CDC checklist ages, AAP Bright Futures edition, and Zero to Three guidance annually; bump minor version for wording, major version for structural changes.

sources.name: CDC 'Learn the Signs. Act Early.' milestone checklists (2022 revision; milestones = what most children, ~75%+, do by that age)
AAP Bright Futures: Guidelines for Health Supervision, 4th ed. (periodicity + anticipatory guidance)
Zero to Three — age-based development and everyday-activity guidance
Harvard Center on the Developing Child — serve-and-return, core capabilities
WHO Motor Development Study — windows of achievement for gross motor milestones

affordanceVocabulary.water_play: Safe water to splash, pour, and observe — high-yield cause-and-effect material
affordanceVocabulary.cause_effect: Objects/exhibits that respond to the child's action (drop, push, splash, press)
affordanceVocabulary.gross_motor_low: Safe surfaces for tummy time, crawling, cruising, early toddling
affordanceVocabulary.climb_run: Open space and low structures for confident walking, running, climbing
affordanceVocabulary.sensory_textures: Varied safe textures, smells, temperatures, sights at child height
affordanceVocabulary.naming_targets: A dense field of distinct, pointable, nameable things (animals, produce, vehicles)
affordanceVocabulary.story_language: Songs, rhymes, books, narrated routines — rich serve-and-return language
affordanceVocabulary.peer_faces: Other babies/children and adults to watch and interact with
affordanceVocabulary.animal_watch: Animals observable at the child's pace and chosen distance
affordanceVocabulary.calm_regulation: Low-stimulation, warm, predictable environments good for co-regulation
affordanceVocabulary.pretend_play: Props and settings that invite imitation and pretend scenarios
affordanceVocabulary.attention_span_long: DEMANDS sustained attention / following a narrative (a cost until ~2.5y, then an affordance)
affordanceVocabulary.rule_games: Games with rules, turn-taking, scores — fair-play and losing-gracefully practice
affordanceVocabulary.big_kid_challenge: Graded physical/skill challenges (bikes, climbing walls, laps, strikes) — measurable mastery
affordanceVocabulary.vehicle_watch: Trains, buses, boats, planes, diggers — moving machines to watch, name, and ride
affordanceVocabulary.snow_play: Snow and ice: sledding, tracks, cold-hands wonder (winter coverage)
affordanceVocabulary.food_ritual: Shared food outings — choosing, tasting, sitting together; ritual and routine
affordanceVocabulary.group_program: Structured drop-in programs with other families (community centre, playgroup, class)
affordanceVocabulary.seasonal_wonder: Seasonal, once-a-year spectacles — blossoms, pumpkins, festivals

bands.label: 0–6 months
bands.theme: Faces, voices, and gentle motion are the whole world. Anywhere calm counts.
bands.caution: Stimulation ceilings are low; leaving early is success, not failure.

bands.label: 6–9 months
bands.theme: Sitting up changes everything — new sightlines, grabbing, and the first cause-and-effect games.
bands.caution: Everything goes in the mouth; choose venues accordingly.

bands.label: 9–12 months
bands.theme: Object permanence and cruising. Peekaboo is science; pulling up on things is the sport.
emergingSkills: understanding simple words; gestures like waving
bands.caution: Newly mobile + zero judgment: floor-level hazard scan is the venue test.

bands.label: 12–15 months
bands.theme: Cause-and-effect play is peaking — splash, drop, watch, repeat. First words are brewing.
emergingSkills: pointing to ask and to share attention
bands.caution: Attention runs in short loops; repetition IS the learning, not a rut.

bands.label: 15–18 months
bands.theme: The pointing-and-naming burst. The world becomes a picture book she wants labeled.
bands.caution: Prime window to RETRY previously failed outings — the same aquarium is a new place now.

bands.label: 18–24 months
bands.theme: Pretend play sparks, climbing gets serious, and 'again!' becomes a lifestyle.
bands.caution: Big feelings era: exits, snacks, and nap windows shape success more than the venue does.

bands.label: 24–30 months
bands.theme: Two-word sentences, real running, and following simple stories. Group activities start to land.
emergingSkills: parallel play shifting toward interactive play
bands.caution: Wild variance in language pace here is normal; never surface comparisons.

bands.label: 30–42 months
bands.theme: Why-questions, imaginative worlds, and longer attention. 'Real' museums start paying off.
emergingSkills: following a simple narrative or show
bands.caution: This is where science centres, theatre, and exhibit museums flip from 'not yet' to 'finally'.

bands.label: 42–60 months
bands.theme: The preschool leap: pretend worlds get plots, questions never stop, and bodies learn to pedal, hop, and truly climb.
emergingSkills: complex pretend narratives and role play
counting and letter curiosity in the wild
bands.caution: Preschool-skill variance is enormous; never compare children.

bands.label: 60–84 months
bands.theme: Big kid, wide world: games with rules, reading hiding everywhere, real museum stamina — and school reshaping the week.
emergingSkills: early reading/numbers applied in the wild
bands.caution: School shifts usage to weekends/holidays; interests individualize — follow the child's leads, not a checklist. LOWER EVIDENCE CONFIDENCE: beyond CDC checklist coverage.

tuningNotes.howToTune: Adjust band 'wants' weights (1–3) based on observed rating patterns across users; never edit emergingSkills to fit engagement metrics — science layer and tuning layer stay separate.
tuningNotes.personalization: Per-child preference signals (loved/paused categories) are applied ON TOP of this map at runtime, never written into it.
